cve_summary: arch/arm64/mm/dma-mapping.c in the Linux kernel before 4.0.3, as used in the ION subsystem in Android and other products, does not initialize certain data structures, which allows local users to obtain sensitive information from kernel memory by triggering a dma_mmap call.
commit_message:
arm64: dma-mapping: always clear allocated buffers

Buffers allocated by dma_alloc_coherent() are always zeroed on Alpha,
ARM (32bit), MIPS, PowerPC, x86/x86_64 and probably other architectures.
It turned out that some drivers rely on this 'feature'. Allocated buffer
might be also exposed to userspace with dma_mmap() call, so clearing it
is desired from security point of view to avoid exposing random memory
to userspace. This patch unifies dma_alloc_coherent() behavior on ARM64
architecture with other implementations by unconditionally zeroing
allocated buffer.

Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # v3.14+
Signed-off-by: Marek Szyprowski <m.szyprowski@samsung.com>
Signed-off-by: Will Deacon <will.deacon@arm.com>
docstring:
/******************************************************************************  
 * Summary:  
 * Allocates memory from a specified pool and returns a pointer to the allocated  
 * memory. If the pool is not initialized, it logs a warning and returns NULL.  
 *  
 * Parameters:  
 * size (size_t): The size of memory to allocate from the pool.  
 * ret_page (struct page **): A pointer to a page pointer where the allocated  
 * page will be stored.  
 * flags (gfp_t): Allocation flags that control the behavior of the allocation.  
 *  
 * Returns:  
 * void *: A pointer to the allocated memory, or NULL if allocation fails or the  
 * pool is not initialized.  
 *  
 * Logic:  
 * The function checks if the atomic pool is initialized. If not, it logs a  
 * warning and returns NULL. If initialized, it attempts to allocate memory of  
 * the specified size from the pool, retrieves the physical address, sets the  
 * corresponding page, and zeroes the allocated memory before returning the  
 * pointer.  
 ******************************************************************************/
extraction_reason: vulnerable-side scope spans 2 top-level constructs (functions/declarations), not a single function
